summary: Crash and/or data corruption upon attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks
description: The bug Attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks causes the player to be unable to respawn. The game crashes (Exception generating new chunk caused by java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and/or the world is corrupted (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException: null), and you become unable to open it again. "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)" is spammed to the debug log. To reproduce 1. Create a new world. 2. Execute /worldborder center 50000000 50000000. 3. Execute /kill. 4. You are unable to respawn. 5. Attempt to go to title screen. 6. The game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new world.
2. Execute `/worldborder center 50000000 50000000`.
3. Execute `/kill`.
4. Attempt to respawn and observe that you are unable to do so.
5. Try to go back to the title screen.
6. Observe that the game crashes or becomes unable to open the world again.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w41a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 21w44a, 1.18 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks, players are unable to respawn and the game crashes due to an exception generating new chunks caused by a java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Additionally, the world becomes corrupted (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException: null), making it impossible to open again. The debug log is spammed with "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)." To reproduce this issue, create a new world and execute `/worldborder center 50000000 50000000`. Then, use the `/kill` command to kill the player. Upon attempting to respawn or return to the title screen, the game crashes or the world becomes unusable. This behavior consistently results in corruption and prevents further interaction with the affected world.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks, the game should function normally without crashing or corrupting the world. The player should be able to respawn and navigate back to the title screen seamlessly. No exceptions or errors should occur during chunk generation or file operations, ensuring that the world remains accessible and playable.
